transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes, I do have a few questions. First, I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a great question! You can start doing light gardening about 1 week after your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the clarification. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, if you need a new supply, your GP should be able to provide some more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light right now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, that's quite normal! It's common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I understand, thank you. My last question is, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was a little over a week ago. It sounds like some blurriness is still normal around this time, so that's good to know. I appreciate your answers to my questions. I don't have anything else to ask right now. Thank you!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Before we finish, can I just confirm - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
